observations: Photo 0: bell-housing/torque-converter end of an automatic transmission, sitting on bare ground outdoors, wiring harness and a sensor plug visible, no legible tag or part number.
Photo 1: side view of the transmission case, dust and dirt coating it, a label/tag is visible on the case but the text is too small/blurred to read, red paint marks typical of yard-sorted used parts.
Photo 2: transmission case separated from the torque converter, input shaft and splines exposed, no serial plate or part sticker legible in this view either.
No shot shows a readable VIN, part number, or stamped transmission code anywhere in the three photos.
No video, fluid-check, or spin-test shown; item is static and outdoors in all shots.

identity.kind: automatic transmission/gearbox assembly, seller claims fitment for a Mercedes-Benz M272 engine

claims.evidence: M272 is a Mercedes-Benz engine code, not a transmission/gearbox code; no plate or stamped part number is legible in any photo to confirm which actual transmission this is.
No shipping label, customs paperwork, or container photo shown.
No video of bench test, no sound clip; photos show a static disassembled unit only.
No donor vehicle odometer or history document shown.
Photo 2 shows the torque converter pulled out of the bell housing with the input shaft and internal splines exposed, meaning the unit has been taken apart at least to this extent.

risks.risk: Exact transmission model/part number cannot be confirmed, which determines fitment and price tier.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped ID plate/tag on the case (visible but unreadable in photo 1).
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unidentified generic used automatic transmission, lowest tier for the claimed engine family

risks.risk: Internal clutch packs, valve body, and mechatronic unit condition unknown; 'no knock' is an audio claim with no evidence.
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being spun or bench-tested with audible sound, or a shop diagnostic printout.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / needing full internal inspection

risks.risk: Torque converter condition (seized, worn lock-up clutch, or leaking) cannot be judged from a static photo.
risks.proof: Video of the torque converter spinning freely plus a weight/fluid-drain check.
risks.if_unproven: priced as suspect/unverified, treated as needing replacement

risks.risk: Seals and gaskets may be dried out or cracked from sitting outdoors on bare ground, risking fluid leaks after installation.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all seal surfaces and the drain plug area.

risks.risk: Import/origin and mileage claims (Tokunbo, Belgium, low mileage) cannot be checked remotely and inflate price if false.
risks.proof: Import/customs documentation or donor-vehicle registration papers.
risks.if_unproven: priced without any premium for claimed origin or mileage

proof_requests: Clear, well-lit close-up of the ID/data plate or stamped part number on the transmission case.
Video of the unit being spun or bench-tested, with audible sound to check for knocking.
Photos of all seal and gasket surfaces, plus the fluid pan and drain plug.
Any import/customs paperwork or donor vehicle documentation supporting the Belgium/Tokunbo claim.
response.reason: The seller's own model label (M272, an engine code, not a transmission code) cannot be matched to any legible part number or ID plate in the photos, so even a worst-case price cannot be anchored to the correct transmission family; a clear tag/plate photo is needed before pricing.
